response: {"title":"Shared-contract closure","intervention":"Whenever a requirement changes a shared function, class, schema, or configuration contract, update its definition, every statically discoverable Python consumer, and its focused tests as one bounded change.","claim":"On matched deadline-limited multi-module Python tasks, appending this contract-closure instruction will increase complete pass_rate versus no appended instruction with median wall_time and turns no more than 15% higher.","mechanism":"Treating shared contracts as an indivisible change unit prevents partial implementations in which a central definition changes but dispersed consumers or validations retain the old behavior.","assumptions":["Cross-module requirements commonly propagate through discoverable shared contracts.","Static search finds the consumers relevant to the task."],"risks":["Dynamic consumers may remain undiscovered.","Updating every apparent consumer can expand scope beyond the deadline.","Bundling tests with implementation may encourage tests that merely confirm the chosen design."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly allocate matched Python tasks involving shared contracts to identical fixed-deadline agents with this appended instruction or no appended instruction.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment all-requirements pass_rate is higher while its median wall_time and turns each stay within 115% of control."},"single_shot_ordinal":11}
